en: With the earth as bowl, the overflowing sea as oil
the [sun] with hot rays as lamp I put [this]
word garland on the feet of him with the red-glowing discus
saying, ‘may I leave the ocean of affliction.’
When was the ocean churned? Which earth did you receive along with water?
Not even one thing I do understand. On that day that was the ocean
you blocked, burst [and on which] you closed [your] eyes, this
is the earth you created, dug up, ate [and] spit out
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Placing one foot upto the measure of the earth, he stretched to go
with one foot upto the measure of the water that envelops the earth, the great lord
who saw the measure of the demon in fearful form. I don’t know
a path to see your measure
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: He who stood as the very portal to the path, by closing the portal of
the senses that are five, [which is] the battle door, [him] Hara knows
in whose throat the poison rests, who that day taught
the Dharma to the Four in the shade of the banyan
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: Hara [and] Nāraṇa the names, bull [and] bird the mounts
the words Sūtra [and] Veda, the temple they live in mountain [and] water
the deeds destruction [and] care, in [their] hands spear [and] discus
the forms flame [and] cloud, [but their] body one
I who cannot forget anything, will I today forget
him with the colour of the flood water, you wretches? That day
lying inside the womb as an embryo, I folded [my] hands in devotion, I looked
in the direction of Tiruvaraṅkam’s resident
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: The directions, the gods of the directions and all the rites
pertaining to the gods [are] a confusion created by him
with the colour of the rain flood who churned the ocean
tall Māl, Kaṇṇaṉ of inexhaustible fame
In order to confuse [the enemy], putting the right-spiralling conch to [your] mouth
why did you, Tirumāl, hide with a chariot wheel in [all]-encompassing
battle the [sun] with attacking rays that moves along the sky
fighting with [your] hand [holding] the battle discus?
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: That day she rested on one of your tusks, isn’t it, of you who entered as a boar
with fighting-tusks [and] rooted [it] up, the earth which you measured
in huge form, extending your feet red [like] broad-leaved [lotuses]
so that the directions trembled, the sky swayed?
gloss: participial noun, dative, perfective aspect, singular, second person
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Earth, mountain, churning sea, wind and sky
were swallowed that day, they say truthfully, by you
with the discus whose fame is seen as of incalculable measure
Is it of this world’s measure, your mouth?
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
pronominalised noun, dative, singular, second person

en: The mouth will praise none but him; the hands will fold for
none but him who stretched over the world; except for the name and the form
of him who ate as food the poison from the breast of the demoness
the eyes won’t see, the ears won’t hear
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The five sense organs, namely ear, mouth, eye, nose, body, the five
elements, [namely] red fire, earth, wind, water, sky, unending
knowledge, sacrifice and good Dharma, they say
are the nature of him who stood as a boar
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, dative, perfective aspect

en: While the immortals by nature, who make an effort
to go to the feet of him with naturally lush tulsi
recite according to the rule, as is natural, [and] revere through observances
he stands [there] as the beginning
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, honorific, third person
participial noun, honorific, third person, perfective aspect

en: All of those people praising in ways known to each of them
saying ‘this one [or] this one is our great lord,’ by painting on the wall
[and] keeping [an icon] they all worship the form that measured
the world as the first of forms
Just the Three will be first. Among those three
the one with the colour of mighty water is the first. Except for the grace
of the good one who is the first, in the world [surrounded by] ample waters
vain [are] the graces of many
gloss: imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: Afraid that all the many days had gone in vain
I wept. Seeing [him] on the serpent bed, I worshipped
the foot of him the colour of the deadly flood [with] red eyes
who rests while the tide of the sea laps at [his] feet
While [his] foot crossed the earth, while [his] arms went out to the directions
his head measured the sky, they say, he who with shapely nails
clawed the chest of Hiraṇya, he who mounted on the large-winged bird
at the time he measured the world
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: The one who ate poison from the drooping breast [and] ate the butter
when it appeared in the netting, he who, pressing down [and] fighting the bull elephant intent on victory
[finally] saw [it] break, and who tore the bird’s mouth
is Māl who went between the myrobalan trees [and] measured the world
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: O perturbed black ocean, what [penance] did you undergo?
to have obtained [the right] to always touch [his] sacred body
during the sleep of Māl with a beautiful black body [and] red eyes
the one with the discus who, having eaten the world, sleeps on a banyan leaf
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Having returned so that the bonds of those who begot [him] loosened, in the form
of a dwarf, red-eyed Māl who crossed the earth of the enemy
folding hands before [his] good lotus-flower red feet the celestials
praise steadily with blossoms in rows
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Red-eyed Māl who stood [and] lifted the Lady Earth from the water
who went [and] with three steps measured the directions, approach
the feet of him who always has the discus as a weapon, the bird as [his] vehicle
the serpent as a bed; immerse yourself, heart, [and] know [them]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: All the world knows, not only me
o you who mounted Suparṇa with spotted wings
about the scars [obtained] when [she with] bamboo-like soft shoulders scented
with perfume tied you, who had eaten the churned butter, with a rope
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
participial noun, accusative, perfective aspect, singular, second person

en: Scarred were the palms that had touched the Śārṅga bow string
scarred were the feet, having kicked the cart, scarred were
the fingers of him the colour of the swelling flood who dug into the chest
of him named after gold, so that she with the flower garland was frightened
At the time when, seeing the butter that had moistened [your] mouth and fingers
the cowherdess fettered [you] close to a mortar, were you not
wailing, [your] voice unceasing, [and] thinking [of it], for the neighbours to see?
O you the colour of the rising flood, tell [me]
Taking up words, my heart, without stopping, always
rises praising him who, like the emerald on the mountain
rested on the waves, who tore open [Hiraṇya’s chest]
who dug up the earth as a boar
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect

en: Vēṅkaṭam that extinguishes the flame of the karma
of those who rise, who take leave, who thoughtfully worship
daily in a faultless manner the one with lush tulsi
is the mountain that kindles the flame of the celestials’ minds
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Covering [the world] with a mountain as umbrella, tearing open the mouth of the horse
destroying with the bow seven Cadamba trees the hands
of him who seized the clouded peak are those that broke the battle tusk
of the murderous elephant and that bent the flowering wild lime tree
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: In [your] hands the right-spiralling conch and the discus, o lord of
cloud colour. The Lady of the flower is on your chest. The righteous
Veda expert [comes] from your navel. The lord who aimed at the three
great fortifications has a seat on your body
The lord, the ground, the dark sky, the wind
the dashing flood, and the red fire is he. See red-eyed Māl
who warded off with care the misery suffered by the green-eyed
big elephant with crescent tusks, [and] understand
gloss: imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: The thoughts of those who straighten [their] minds, so as to be clear
[and] easily [and] well understand knowledge, like a calf
that easily finds [its] mother, go to the feet of him with cool tulsi
[and] desirously seek [them] out
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Grasping in one hand the conch, holding in the other the golden discus
being in lion form and in man form, Māl who dug up the chest
of him with flame[-like] beautiful colour, is it possible to regard
something other than his feet, [even] for a moment?
Those who, looking with unblinking eyes so that the darkness departs
properly hold tight in [their] chests the five senses
so that they don’t torment, they will reach the town of him
on the bed of the snake with a thousand mouths
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Not thinking with the mind anything but the names of the excellent one
who graced the four-faced one with an abode on the flower
[and] produced the splendid Vedas, what benefit is there
that comes from [praying at] dusk and dawn, when one recites [and] counts repetitions?
Why? Some people call ‘truth’ o you of cloud colour
who once was alone on the banyan leaf after you had eaten the seven worlds
the way [your] cowherd mother with big beautiful eyes gave [you her] breast
when the demonic mother, who meltingly gave you [her] breast, did not move [anymore]
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, feminine, perfective aspect

en: Don’t take amiss what has been said with affection
by [your] servants of undiminished love. Was the hostility
shown by the one with twice five heads (Rāvaṇa) not clearly
in order to reach the feet of you, Tall one?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Was it in order to destroy the strength of hostility, once
when the earth was his alone, the manner you asked for
yourself the earth, with [your] hand [that holds] the golden discus
with the sharp nails that had wounded Hiraṇya?
Vēṅkaṭam, where Veda experts arrive from all directions [and] bow
offering lamps with incense and water with flowers
daily, those who acquire the subtle aural teachings without division
is the place that delights Māl, with [his] mouth that blew the white conch
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, honorific, third person

en: Vēṅkaṭam, where the crawling striped snake perceives the big gem
thrown by the illustrious hill people, so that the big elephant moves on
as the lightning of the monsoon rain [and] reaches the ant hill
is the place of Māl of which the gods above say ‘ours’
Digging up the earth, lifting the mountain
prevailing over Kaṃsa, once to be feared
lying on the great ocean with water floods and standing on Vēṅkaṭam
is what is great in the one the colour of the great flood
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Vēṅkaṭam
where the bull elephant that had abandoned the field, frightened
by the red fire in the hands of the hill people with arrows in big bows
is [now] afraid upon seeing stars fall from the dark sky
is the hill of the one who once delighted in seeing the king of the Asuras fall
From today onwards, o my heart
that takes it for merit, even if it commits a fault as [big] as a mountain
always keep thinking of words on the matter
of him in whose hand is the golden discus, even if it is but slanderous words
When the Lady Śrī, the earth lady and the cowherd lady join [him]
what is [this] way that it stops at the Lady Śrī
the mind of him with the colour of the dark flood
who rested on the hooded-serpent bed while the milk flood is spilled on Śrī?
Blemishes of the mind will end, and difficult karma will not approach
As wealth it will prosper of those people of his
who keep worshipping, offering water along with buds to the feet
of him with flowering tulsi from the fields
Whatever form delights his people is just the form
whatever name delights his people again is the name, whatever colour
his people delightedly keep thinking of without blinking
that is the colour of him with the discus
gloss: participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter singular, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: There are things not known to the immortals. Let that rest
We, we can know [them], good heart [those] qualities of the one who counted
with [his] feet the tall heads of the Rākṣasa with a sword who had humbled
himself at the feet of the one with great penance who resides in the flower
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Those who humble themselves at the feet of him with a chest that he wounded
so to end the karma of the one with a white sacred thread on his chest
who accepted gifts in the skull of the one with four Vedas he intoned
see, will rule the earth along with [enjoying] the pleasures of the immortals
gloss: imperfective aspect, plural, third person, noun

en: Those who understand with sharp true knowledge, keeping straight
all the five rutting elephants (the senses) so as not to roam the streets
by lessening the [musth] water, they will see the anklet[ed] feet of the one
who protected the elephant on a former day
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Join in going to the red feet of him who held up the flaming battle discus
on one hand, for the agitated gods and Asuras to be afraid
with the other hand lifting [Namuci] by one foot [and] spinning [him] around
Immerse yourself in joy, heart!
Except for those who exert themselves so that [their] bodies are so
emaciated that [they] alter to the likeness of a single makiḻ-seed
it is difficult for those who [want to] see our First cause with the high
crown of glowing gold that appears like a blooming radiance
gloss: participial noun, present tense, dative, plural, third person
participial noun, dative, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: If one embraces [him] by means of practising devotion
with choice flowers, repressing the five senses difficult [to control]
it is easy to see the one who received in [his] generous hand water
from Māvali who unchangeably sat enthroned as a great man
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: In order to easily see [his] two [feet] when my mind becomes clear
[they] remain fully clear count the holy names
of him who was [here] as a lion, taking up the fight
against the one who was improper in [his] pride
gloss: neuter singular, dative, imperfective aspect, verbal noun
participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, negative
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: As the Eight, the Eleven, the Twelve [and] the Two approach
offering beautiful blossoms daily
[and] revere [him] with a singular garland, without ever stopping
they go [and] worship Tirumāl with hands [folded]
When He goes it is [his] parasol, when He sits it is [his] lion throne
when He stands it is [his] sandals, in the large ocean always
it is [his] raft, [his] jewel lamp is it, [and his] beautiful silk garment, the bed
where He embraces [Śrī] is Tirumāl’s serpent
The one who, without hiding, sent the snake, broke the murderous bull elephant
grazed the cows, broke the wild lime tree, tore the bird’s beak, linked [hands]
in the Kuravai dance, danced with the pots, drank from the breast [of the demoness]
killed the wrestlers [and] lifted the hill, is him with red eyes
‘His people, whatever [their] karma, are our king’s people,’
apart from being left with that thought, they do not know
of being examined by Yama’s people, see, those named
servants of the great cowherd on the serpent bed
gloss: neuter singular, imperfective aspect, verbal noun
pronominalised noun, instrumental, plural, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Besides babbling so that just [his] names come [out], who will be those
who know our Lord? Let that rest. [Even] the Unborn one
despite sitting in the fragrant lotus, cannot directly see
the foot lotuses of Kaṇṇaṉ
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: I was afraid of the harsh karma that stood nearby. Having been afraid
in order to join your holy feet so that I escape [fear]
worshipping with a favoured good [flower] garland, I have learned
the word garland saying ‘obeissance, oh Nāraṇaṉ’
Let us rise, worshipping, taking flowers, offering incense
with [our] hands, rise, oh heart. Mantras that are learned
without fault in order to worship with the hands the feet of Māl
there is no end [of them]. Reach [them]
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, imperfective aspect

en: If [you] want that jumble of unhappiness, pain [and] evil, along with the difficult karma
that has settled [on you], to stop returning, [your] refuge is the one
who put [his] palm to his bow on a former day so that the opposition of him
who once had placed in Laṅkā [her with] a swaying waist, was destroyed
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect

en: It does not know any other lord than the one who took the big discus
as protection for all living beings who are mortal
along with him from the lotus who yielded the Vedas as a refuge
[this] world surrounded by one ocean
The world and the aeons, during which the world expires, and in the world
the receding black ocean with bright lustre, the mountains
red fire, the wind and the sky are the creation
that comes into existence in the mind of Tirumāl
After going between the joined myrobalan trees, bending down the flowering wild lime tree
[and] subduing the seven huge bulls in order to unite in marriage
they leapt over the seven worlds so that the hosts [of Asuras] were frightened
and went into all eight directions, the arms of him on the undulating bed
of the serpent that envelops [him]
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: [My] arms worship none but him. My two ears keep listening
to the sweet words of him who is kin. [My] tongue’s daily
talking of the jangling anklets of him on the bed of the murderous serpent
is the devotion of me who does not associate with shamelessness
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
imperfective aspect, verbal noun, neuter singular
participial noun, negative, singular, first person

en: I shan’t desire the wealth of others, I shan’t associate with low people
I shan’t consult any but elevated people, I shan’t wonder at
[and] I shan’t praise as god any but Tirumāl
What would be the way that karma comes upon us?
gloss: pronominalised noun, sociative, plural, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, sociative, plural, third person

en: They shall not be oppressed by karma, they shall not join hot hell
they shall not, even by a trifle, go on evil paths when they [fold
their] hands in worship of the black one with red eyes, with a thousand names
the distant one, the one who is difficult to think of
What is learned by the world, as it rises in the morning, and what is listened to
are the names of the one who took the great discus. What is desired and sung
by the highest brahmins who had before understood [and] learned [them]
are the feet of the one on the sea with a unique discus
gloss: participial noun, neuter plural, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, neuter plural, imperfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: The river looks towards the moving black sea. The bright flower
looks towards the One with rays who rises. All living beings
look towards the one who has Dharma. The intellect looks towards the One
the husband of her on the bright lotus
gloss: pronominalised noun, masculine singular, third person

en: Who are those who perceive your greatness aeon after aeon?
Who are those who perceive your form? You who are in heaven
who are on the earth, you who are on Vēṅkaṭam, you who are in the melodies
of the four Vedas, who are those that perceive the milk [sea] you lie on?
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: They speak of the body in which you slumbered on a banyan leaf, having
on a former day, in the form of a boy eaten the seven worlds. The leaf, on that day
was it in the flood, the water of the ocean? was it in heaven, was it on earth?
You who lifted the mountain enveloped by groves, speak
As long as there is speech, worship [him]. As long as the body that will fall
[still] goes on, it is good if you praise Tirumāl with strands
of good petals, with sacrifice, with ritual acts
with mantras [and] with names
Even though he has well abolished illness and old age
[and] steadily rules the whole earth through the four aeons, always
immerse yourself in letting go , heart. I wanted, see
love from him who took the deadly discus
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect

en: Love says ‘approach him with the discus’. The tongue says
‘laud [and] praise the arm of him with the excellent discus.’ ‘See him
who did not see earlier aeons,’ says the eye. The ear says ‘listen
to the praises of him who wore the ornamental wreath.’
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: You praise, you blame, you slight, you ponder
him with the flowering tulsi, my heart him
who held the sea, the mountain, the vast sky
the wind, the bodies and [their life] breaths
gloss: pronominalised noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: He with the bull, he mounted on the bird, he who burned the forts
he who dug open the chest, he with ashes, he with shady sapphire colour
he with the woman on one half side, he with the Lady of the flower
he with flowing matted hair, he with the tall crown, he with the Gaṅgā
he with the long anklets [stands] guard
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: When one considers you as protection, the difficult karmas pass
When one considers you, the bonds open [and] vanish. For those
who ponder you, there is no old age, Tirumāl. Those who praise
your feet will see the way
gloss: participial noun, dative, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Those who are steady on the way [and] worship you will be of a form
that stands by unfailing words. In a manner
that not a single mistake occurs it gives heavens
holy Vēṅkaṭam of the Excellent one who measured the earth
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: ‘Vēṅkaṭam, the heavenly city, Veḵkā and the large golden city
of Kōval, with a moat of unwithering flowers, in [those] four places
he stood, he sat, he lay, he walked;’
when one says so, affliction gets destroyed
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, singular, masculine, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Who are those that [still] suffer affliction? Rise, heart! We will worship
with [our] hands the feet of him with a hooded green snake as [his] bed
who aimed at the very cruel crocodile that clung to the bull elephant
taking buds of [freshly] plucked Nāka flowers
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Other than the one who took, who will blame the one who gave?
Did you not beg Māvali ‘give [me] earth’ [and], when water
in a clear stream touched [your] palm, approach [and] stretch out
[your] precious palm to reach for the lofty skies?
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, accusative, perfective aspect
participial noun, accusative, perfective aspect, plural, third person

en: Running, having thought ‘I can’t bear [to serve] the harsh enemies who approached’
are there servants except for [those] of the cunning one with dark body
who gave into the hand of the strong one the poisonous snake
that surrounded the firm big city?
The name of him, isn’t it, who churned by setting up the mountain
coiling [around it] the long snake, wanting a fight for glory
that day on the victorious battle field abounding in men
is the weapon that grips [and] drives away old hell
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect

en: Vēṅkaṭam, that magically absorbs stains, so that the stars vanish
in between the incense offered together with strands of fresh flowers
on the twelveth day by those with sword eyes that they wear as weapons
is the mountain of him who on a former day took aim with great magic
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Which was the way that he protected the herd of cows with the mountain as an umbrella
[and his] arm as a shaft [and] subdued the seven bulls from the herds of the cowherds
the lord who, lying in the ocean with powerful water, took up the big discus
against the hostile night-wandering [demons]?
O lord, who else will be [among] those who know your greatness?
At the time you stretched [and] measured the world, in which way, my father
did she not reach up to the measure of the boar’s tusks
the earth that reached up to the measure of [your] feet?
Can you see [and] know [his] body? Can you see [and] know
the bird banner of him on the snake bed? Speak, you
oh heart that controls the five senses inside the body, offers water
along with buds [and] stays on the path
You stand there, you and the Lady Śrī, o excellent man who lifted
the mountain and concealed from the spreading water
without passing by the entrance, without entering inside
now holding on to the entry hall of Kōval
Who will now enter the gate to the seven hells? Without disgust, close
the strong bar. For seeing the [feet with] tinkling anklets of him
with the arms that threw the calf so that the fruit perished
[there] is the well-known Nāvala land surrounded [by the sea]
gloss: neuter singular, dative, imperfective aspect, verbal noun

en: When I search, I search your feet. When daily
I sing, I sing your praise. To me who, if I wear [anything]
wear the gold[-ringed] feet of him who raised the golden discus
if anything should happen to me, what [of it]?
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
participial noun, dative, imperfective aspect, singular, first person

en: Who else would be there for me? My great lord
alone exists for himself. Besides, when I see the complexion
of iron-wood flowers in the field, of bilberry flowers
that open [their] buds, [they are] a boon that show [his] dark body
gloss: imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: O Mātavaṉ, saying to yourself that it is thinking of [his] strength
because of the boon that he did not bow with [his] head before your feet
as a unique lion, you dug into the flesh of Hiraṇya who was not to be seized
directly, as an enemy dragged by [your] strength
gloss: neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: He of the aeons who entered into covers of flesh, dispelled
the darkness, kindled the flame of cognition every day
who in the form of a boar dug out the world, is it that there is
heaven [even] for those who don’t join [his] feet?
gloss: participial noun, dative, negative, plural, third person

en: O Tirumāl who is sky, fire, churning sea, wind
honey [and] milk, when you swallow the butter
of the cowherdess, will it be full, [that] belly that
on a former day, spit out the earth?
Did you suck [his blood] with [your] mouth, so that [your] teeth shone terrifyingly
him who had come in the form of light, so that [his] belly burned
o you with the golden discus in [your] hand that degraded [its] flower form by tainted nails
destroying [him] so that he lost [his] strength on your red feet?
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, perfective aspect
neuter singular, perfective aspect, verbal noun

en: Opening [my] mouth [with the words] ‘are these again these seven worlds
that went on being destroyed, rising [and] looking into the eye of fire?’
my tongue praises no lord except for the cunning one who showed
himself wholly to the Veda expert
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: There is a tongue in the mouth. There is speech that says
incessantly ‘obeisance, oh Nāraṇaṉ’. There is a means
to go the ageless great way. How can
someone go onto the path of evil?
My heart, unswervingly see red-eyed Māl
He is both merit and evil. He is outside
this earth, the churning sea, the wind, the sky is he
see, [he is] a hold at the end
gloss: imperfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: O great man who took care of the bull elephant joined with [its] female
joining your feet she obtained grace, did she not, [that] gold with the name
called Gaṅgā, the stream that flows down on the shining matted hair of him
who received the fire in [his] palm, joined with ashes?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: The body glittering with gold: the virtuous one with matted locks
and tall Māl who constantly extends the world, even if
they always wander around with a body of two, always
one is present in the body of the other
He is, see, good heart, the highest. Always
he is, see, in the heart of those who remember [him]. He is, see
the one inside the ocean and resident on Vēṅkaṭam
Realise: ‘he is inside [your] heart.’
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, plural, third person
participial noun, perfective aspect, singular, masculine, third person

en: One foot that kicked the cart and a bright red flower foot
two feet are there to see, my heart. Towards the one who extended
one foot, Kēcavaṉ, the cunning one joined by a garland
of cool tulsi direct your mind
gloss: participial noun, masculine singular, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
